units.function: HTTP tests for serving a ready plugin's built UI assets publicly and optionally proxying a Company-configured development UI origin after authentication and tenant access checks.
units.dependencyDirection: Plugin registry packagePath/manifest UI entrypoint and optional Company devUiUrl feed an Express static/proxy route under the Paperclip server origin; browser-loaded JavaScript is authored by the plugin package.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin ID/key/package path/version/status/UI entrypoint; static asset path/body; board actor Company IDs; Company config devUiUrl; development environment; proxied content type.
units.lifecycle: Resolve a ready plugin; serve built UI JavaScript without Company context; or authenticate and authorize Company access, read devUiUrl and proxy the requested asset during development.
units.testAssessment: All four tests pass outside the restricted sandbox and Company gating for dev configuration is explicit. The security surface is otherwise largely untested: path encoding/traversal/symlinks, disabled/uninstalled state, asset integrity/version/cache, MIME/nosniff, CSP/CORS/CORP, source maps/size, dev proxy SSRF/redirects/timeouts and browser privilege isolation. Public availability is not itself the main issue; executing untrusted plugin code under the customer application's origin would grant ambient Web privileges unless separately isolated.
units.designRationale: Let installed plugins contribute UI bundles with simple stable asset URLs and support hot local development without rebuilding the main Web application.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS owns an independent Chinese/Raft-style Web and must not allow third-party pages or scripts to become a second same-origin customer UI or inherit authenticated browser authority.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT direct same-origin plugin UI bundles and arbitrary devUiUrl proxying. Prefer headless server/Connector capabilities projected through Company OS-owned UI. If a third-party UI is indispensable, serve immutable signed assets from a separate uncredentialed origin inside a sandboxed iframe with no same-origin permission, strict CSP/CORP, explicit postMessage schema/capabilities, short-lived audience tokens and user-visible provenance. Development proxying is local-only with loopback allowlist, redirect denial and prominent unsafe mode. Never reuse upstream full page components or business copy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Same-origin plugin JavaScript can potentially act with the logged-in human's browser authority while obscuring which code initiated a decision. That undermines independent identity audiences and the evidence-backed responsibility chain.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL browser trust gap: no test proves plugin JavaScript is isolated from the authenticated application origin, cookies, storage or APIs. HIGH supply-chain gap: asset signature/hash/version integrity and disabled/uninstalled behavior are absent. HIGH path/content gap: traversal/symlink, MIME sniffing, CSP/CORS/CORP, source-map and size controls are untested. HIGH development SSRF gap: configurable devUiUrl proxy lacks tested scheme/host/redirect confinement. MEDIUM cache risk: immutable versioned URLs, revocation and rollback behavior are absent. POSITIVE: dev config is not read before authentication and Company access checks.
